metadata.description: Universal medical disease database covering all major body systems

general_diseases.name: Pneumonia
general_diseases.description: Infection of the lung parenchyma causing consolidation and impaired gas exchange. Leading cause of death worldwide and a major cause of hospitalisation in India.
treatments: Mild CAP: oral Amoxicillin 1g 3 times daily for 5-7 days OR Doxycycline
Moderate: oral Co-amoxiclav + Clarithromycin
Severe: IV Ceftriaxone + IV Azithromycin / Clarithromycin
Supplemental oxygen if SaO2 <94%
Adequate hydration
Paracetamol for fever/pain
Physiotherapy
Atypical pneumonia: Azithromycin or Doxycycline
prevention: Pneumococcal vaccine (PCV13/PPSV23) for elderly and at-risk

general_diseases.name: Asthma
general_diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory airway disease with reversible bronchoconstriction, causing episodic wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness, and cough. Extremely prevalent in India affecting 6% of adults and 10% of children.
symptoms: Symptoms triggered by allergens, exercise, cold, infections
causes: Allergic (atopic): dust mites, pollen, pet dander, mould
Non-allergic: exercise, cold air, infections, stress, aspirin/NSAIDs
Air pollution (common trigger in Indian cities)
treatments: Reliever: Salbutamol MDI 100-200mcg (2 puffs) as needed — use spacer
Preventer: Inhaled corticosteroids (Budesonide/Beclometasone/Fluticasone) daily
LABA: Salmeterol or Formoterol added if poorly controlled
Leukotriene receptor antagonist: Montelukast — popular in India
Acute severe: high-dose salbutamol nebuliser + IV hydrocortisone + oxygen
Avoid triggers (dust, mould, smoking, cockroaches)
warning_signs: Peak flow not improving after reliever

general_diseases.name: Tuberculosis (TB)
general_diseases.description: India has the world's highest TB burden — 2.6 million cases per year. Pulmonary TB is most common but extrapulmonary forms (lymph node, spinal, meningeal, abdominal) are frequent in India. Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) is a growing crisis.
symptoms: Cough >2 weeks (productive, may have blood — haemoptysis)
Pleural effusion (TB pleurisy — chest pain, breathlessness)
Lymph node swelling (cervical most common in extrapulmonary)
treatments: Standard 6-month DOTS regimen: 2HRZE/4HR (Isoniazid + Rifampicin + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol for 2 months, then Isoniazid + Rifampicin for 4 months)
MDR-TB: longer regimen with second-line drugs (bedaquiline, linezolid)
XDR-TB: specialist centre only
Free treatment available under India's Nikshay programme
Give Pyridoxine (B6) with Isoniazid to prevent neuropathy
prevention: BCG vaccination at birth (Indian national programme)

general_diseases.name: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
general_diseases.description: Progressive irreversible airflow obstruction predominantly from emphysema and chronic bronchitis. Massive burden in India from biomass fuel exposure (cooking fires), tobacco, and occupational dust. Often undiagnosed until advanced.
symptoms: Cor pulmonale (right heart failure — ankle oedema)
causes: Biomass fuel exposure (cow dung, wood fires — VERY common in Indian rural women)
treatments: SABA bronchodilator (Salbutamol) + SAMA (Ipratropium) — reliever
LABA (Formoterol, Salmeterol) + LAMA (Tiotropium) — maintenance
Inhaled corticosteroid if frequent exacerbations
Pulmonary rehabilitation
Long-term oxygen therapy if SaO2 <88% at rest
Smoking cessation (most important intervention)
Exacerbations: antibiotics (amoxicillin/doxycycline) + oral prednisolone
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccine
prevention: Reduce biomass fuel exposure (LPG adoption — national programme in India)

general_diseases.name: Influenza (Flu)
general_diseases.description: Acute viral respiratory illness with systemic symptoms. Seasonal epidemics occur regularly in India (monsoon and winter). H1N1 (swine flu) caused major outbreaks in India in 2009 and 2015.
causes: Influenza A (including H1N1, H3N2) or B viruses
treatments: Rest and adequate hydration
Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for fever and pain (NOT Aspirin in children)
Antiviral: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) 75mg twice daily for 5 days — start within 48h; especially for high-risk patients (elderly, pregnant, diabetics, immunocompromised)
Nasal decongestant for congestion
prevention: Annual influenza vaccine (especially recommended in India for elderly, diabetics, cardiac patients, healthcare workers)
Avoid close contact with infected individuals

general_diseases.name: COVID-19
general_diseases.description: Novel coronavirus disease causing respiratory illness from asymptomatic to severe ARDS. India experienced devastating waves in 2020-2022. Long COVID is now a significant healthcare burden.
symptoms: Loss of smell (anosmia) and/or taste (ageusia) — characteristic
Severe disease: hypoxia, ARDS, multi-organ failure
treatments: Mild: Rest, paracetamol, adequate hydration, isolation
Oxygen monitoring with pulse oximeter
Moderate-severe: Supplemental oxygen, IV fluids, Remdesivir (within 7 days), Dexamethasone (if requiring O2)
Anticoagulation (DVT/PE prevention in hospitalised patients)
COVID-19 vaccine booster doses
Long COVID: multidisciplinary rehabilitation
prevention: COVID-19 vaccination (Covishield, Covaxin, Corbevax — Indian vaccines)
red_flags: SaO2 <94% at rest or <90% on exertion

general_diseases.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
general_diseases.description: Persistently elevated blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg). India has 200 million hypertensives — largely undiagnosed and untreated. Biggest preventable cause of stroke and heart attack.
symptoms: Hypertensive urgency/emergency: severe headache, visual changes, chest pain, breathlessness, confusion
causes: Essential hypertension (90%): genetic + lifestyle (salt, obesity, stress, inactivity, alcohol)
Secondary: renal disease (CKD, renovascular), hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, sleep apnoea
treatments: Lifestyle: DASH diet (low salt — WHO target <5g/day), weight loss, exercise, alcohol reduction, smoking cessation
First line drugs: ACE inhibitor (Ramipril) or ARB (Losartan), Calcium Channel Blocker (Amlodipine), Thiazide diuretic (Hydrochlorothiazide)
South Asians respond better to CCB/diuretic combination
Double/triple therapy if uncontrolled
Hypertensive emergency: IV labetalol, nicardipine (hospital)

general_diseases.name: Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
general_diseases.description: Sudden death of heart muscle due to blockage of coronary artery. India sees >5 million heart attacks annually. Indian patients tend to be younger than Western populations and have worse outcomes. A medical emergency requiring immediate hospital treatment.
symptoms: Severe crushing/squeezing central chest pain — may radiate to left arm, jaw, neck, back
Atypical in women/diabetics: fatigue, nausea, jaw pain without chest pain
causes: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture in coronary artery
Risk factors: smoking, hypertension, diabetes (very common in India), dyslipidaemia, family history
treatments: CALL EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY — time is muscle
Aspirin 300mg chewed immediately (if no allergy)
Clopidogrel 300mg loading dose
Oxygen if SaO2 <94%
Nitrates (GTN) for pain (NOT if BP low)
Primary PCI (coronary angioplasty) — within 90 minutes is gold standard
Thrombolysis (streptokinase/tPA) if PCI not available within 120 minutes
Anticoagulation (heparin/enoxaparin)
Beta-blocker, Statin, ACE inhibitor post-MI
prevention: Lifestyle: stop smoking, healthy diet, exercise, weight loss
Control risk factors: BP, diabetes, cholesterol
warning_signs: Any chest pain radiating to arm/jaw

general_diseases.name: Angina
general_diseases.description: Chest pain/discomfort caused by insufficient blood supply to the heart muscle. Stable angina is predictable (on exertion). Unstable angina is a medical emergency (pain at rest or progressively worsening).
symptoms: Radiates to left arm, jaw, or neck
Relieved by rest or GTN within 5 minutes (stable)
Unstable: pain at rest, increasing frequency, not relieved by GTN
treatments: GTN spray under tongue for acute episodes
Beta-blocker (metoprolol) or CCB (amlodipine) for prevention
Long-acting nitrate (isosorbide mononitrate)
Aspirin 75mg + Statin daily
Lifestyle changes
Unstable angina: hospital admission, IV heparin, coronary angiography
red_flags: Unstable angina (rest pain, not resolving) — treat as MI
warning_signs: Chest pain not resolving with GTN in 15 minutes

general_diseases.name: Heart Failure
general_diseases.description: Heart unable to pump sufficient blood to meet body's needs. Common in India from hypertension, rheumatic heart disease (still prevalent), ischaemic heart disease, and dilated cardiomyopathy. Causes significant disability and hospitalisation.
symptoms: Breathlessness on exertion (progressing to breathless at rest)
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (woken at night breathless)
Cough (especially at night, may be frothy/pink in acute pulmonary oedema)
causes: Rheumatic heart disease (common in India — from strep throat)
treatments: ACE inhibitor/ARB (reduces mortality)
Beta-blocker (Carvedilol, Metoprolol)
Spironolactone (aldosterone antagonist)
Diuretics (Furosemide) for fluid removal
SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin — proven mortality benefit)
Device therapy: ICD, CRT pacemaker
Acute pulmonary oedema: IV furosemide, CPAP oxygen, IV nitrates (hospital)
prevention: Treat hypertension and coronary artery disease early
Prevent rheumatic heart disease (treat strep throat with penicillin)
red_flags: Acute pulmonary oedema (severe breathlessness, pink frothy sputum)

general_diseases.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
general_diseases.description: Chronic condition where stomach acid refluxes into oesophagus causing heartburn and regurgitation. Extremely common in India — affects 18-22% of population. Often related to spicy food, obesity, lying down after meals.
symptoms: Heartburn (burning sensation in chest/throat, especially after meals)
Worsened by lying down, bending forward, large meals, spicy food
treatments: Lifestyle changes: elevate bed head, lose weight, avoid trigger foods, no meals 3h before bed
Antacids for immediate relief (Gelusil, Digene — very popular in India)
H2 blockers (Ranitidine, Famotidine)
Proton pump inhibitors (Omeprazole 20mg, Pantoprazole 40mg) — 4-8 weeks
H. pylori eradication if present
Fundoplication surgery for refractory GERD
prevention: Avoid trigger foods (spicy, fatty, coffee, alcohol)
Elevate head of bed if nocturnal symptoms
red_flags: Symptoms not responding to PPI (Barrett's oesophagus)

general_diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
general_diseases.description: Erosion of stomach or duodenal lining causing pain. Very common in India — H. pylori infection (prevalent in 70-80% of adult Indians due to poor sanitation) and NSAID overuse are major causes.
symptoms: Gastric ulcer: pain worse with food
Duodenal ulcer: pain 2-3 hours after meal, at night, relieved by food/antacids
Complication: Vomiting blood (haematemesis), black tarry stools (melaena) — EMERGENCY
causes: NSAID overuse (aspirin, diclofenac, ibuprofen — very common in India)
treatments: H. pylori eradication: Triple therapy — PPI + Clarithromycin + Amoxicillin for 14 days (check local resistance patterns)
Or quadruple therapy in clarithromycin-resistant areas
PPI (Omeprazole 20mg or Pantoprazole 40mg) for 4-8 weeks
Stop NSAIDs and use gastroprotective PPI if NSAID must continue
Antacids for symptom relief
Bleeding ulcer: hospital admission, endoscopy, IV PPI
prevention: Safe drinking water and hand hygiene (reduces H. pylori)
Avoid NSAID overuse — use paracetamol instead
Avoid empty stomach for long periods (duodenal ulcer)
red_flags: Perforation (sudden severe abdominal pain, rigid abdomen) — EMERGENCY

general_diseases.name: Hepatitis B
general_diseases.description: Viral infection of the liver. India has intermediate endemicity (3-4% HBsAg positive). Chronic HBV causes cirrhosis and liver cancer. Mother-to-child transmission is a major route. Vaccine-preventable.
symptoms: Acute: jaundice (yellow eyes/skin), dark urine, pale stools, fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, fever
Chronic: often asymptomatic for years, fatigue, right upper quadrant discomfort
Liver cancer (HCC): weight loss, right upper quadrant mass
causes: Unscreened blood transfusion (risk in some parts of India)
treatments: Acute: supportive (rest, hydration, avoid alcohol)
Chronic: Tenofovir or Entecavir (antiviral, usually lifelong)
Monitor for HCC with 6-monthly ultrasound and AFP
Hepatitis B vaccination if not immune (3-dose schedule)
Interferon-alpha (selected patients)
prevention: Hepatitis B vaccine (included in India's national immunisation schedule)
red_flags: Signs of liver failure: jaundice + encephalopathy + coagulopathy

general_diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
general_diseases.description: Systemic bacterial infection from contaminated food/water. India has one of the highest typhoid burdens globally — ~10 million cases per year. Enteric fever caused by Salmonella typhi or paratyphi.
symptoms: Sustained fever (step-ladder pattern), typically 38-40°C, worsens over week
Rose spots (faint salmon-coloured spots on trunk — pathognomonic)
Relative bradycardia (slow pulse despite high fever)
causes: Salmonella typhi (S. Paratyphi A/B for paratyphoid)
Faecal-oral route through contaminated water and food
treatments: Antibiotics: Ceftriaxone IV 2g daily for 10-14 days (first choice for hospitalised)
Oral: Azithromycin 1g daily for 5-7 days (for mild-moderate)
Or Ciprofloxacin 500mg twice daily for 10-14 days (check sensitivity — resistance growing in India)
Multidrug-resistant (MDR) typhoid: Ceftriaxone or Azithromycin
Adequate hydration and nutrition
Paracetamol for fever
prevention: Safe drinking water (boil, filter, or bottled)
Avoid street food during high-risk periods
Typhoid vaccine (Vi polysaccharide or Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine — Typbar TCV in India)
red_flags: Intestinal perforation (sudden severe abdominal pain, rigid abdomen)
warning_signs: Sudden severe abdominal pain after 2 weeks of fever (perforation)

general_diseases.name: Cholera
general_diseases.description: Acute watery diarrhoea causing severe dehydration. Cholera outbreaks occur in India during floods and monsoons, particularly in resource-poor areas. Rapid fluid loss can be fatal within hours if untreated.
symptoms: Profuse, painless, watery diarrhoea ('rice water' stools)
Sunken eyes, dry mouth, skin turgor loss
Shock in severe cases (low BP, rapid pulse)
treatments: Oral rehydration salts (ORS) — cornerstone, can save life at home
IV fluids (Ringer's lactate) for severe dehydration (hospital)
Antibiotics: Doxycycline 300mg single dose OR Azithromycin 1g single dose (reduce duration and shedding)
Zinc supplementation (especially children)
prevention: Oral cholera vaccine (Shanchol — available in India)

general_diseases.name: Migraine
general_diseases.description: Episodic headache disorder with significant disability. Very common — affects 25% of women and 10% of men. Indian prevalence high due to stress, sleep disruption, and dietary triggers.
symptoms: Aura (in 30%): visual (zigzag lines, flashing lights), sensory, or speech disturbance preceding headache
causes: Triggers: menstruation, sleep changes, stress, alcohol (red wine), tyramine (cheese, chocolate), bright lights, strong smells, missed meals
treatments: Acute: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen 400mg) or Paracetamol + Domperidone for nausea
Triptans: Sumatriptan 50-100mg (or nasal spray/injection) — gold standard for acute moderate-severe migraine
Ergotamine (older, India still uses)
Prevention (if >4/month): Propranolol 40-80mg daily, Topiramate 25-100mg, Amitriptyline 10-25mg, Valproate
Anti-CGRP biologics (Erenumab) for chronic migraine
red_flags: 'Thunderclap headache' (worst headache of life, sudden onset — subarachnoid haemorrhage)
warning_signs: Headache with weakness or vision loss

general_diseases.name: Stroke (CVA)
general_diseases.description: Sudden neurological deficit due to interrupted blood supply to brain (ischaemic) or bleeding into brain (haemorrhagic). TIME IS BRAIN — immediate hospital treatment within 4.5 hours for thrombolysis. India has 1.8 million strokes per year.
symptoms: FAST: Facial drooping (one side), Arm weakness (one side), Speech difficulty/slurring, Time to call emergency
Sudden vision loss or double vision
Sudden unsteadiness or loss of coordination
TIA: Same symptoms but resolving within 24 hours
causes: Ischaemic (80%): thrombosis (in atherosclerotic vessel) or embolism (from AF or carotid disease)
Haemorrhagic (20%): hypertension most common, aneurysm rupture, AVM
Risk factors: hypertension (most modifiable), diabetes, AF, smoking, dyslipidaemia
treatments: EMERGENCY — call ambulance immediately
Ischaemic within 4.5h: IV Alteplase (tPA) thrombolysis
Mechanical thrombectomy up to 24h for large vessel occlusion
Haemorrhagic: control BP, reverse anticoagulation, neurosurgery
Secondary prevention: Aspirin + Clopidogrel (dual antiplatelet), Statin, control BP/diabetes
AF: Anticoagulation (DOAC — Apixaban/Rivaroxaban)
Rehabilitation: physiotherapy, speech therapy
red_flags: EMERGENCY — any stroke symptom requires immediate 112/911 call

general_diseases.name: Epilepsy
general_diseases.description: Recurrent unprovoked seizures. 12 million epileptics in India — second highest worldwide. Neurocysticercosis (tapeworm in brain) is a major cause of epilepsy in India. Stigma remains a significant barrier to treatment in rural India.
symptoms: Tonic-clonic (grand mal): sudden loss of consciousness, body stiffening (tonic), then rhythmic jerking (clonic), post-ictal confusion
Absence: brief staring spells, unresponsive for seconds, no falling
Focal: limited to one area — jerking of one limb, speech arrest, automatisms
Status epilepticus: seizure lasting >5 minutes or multiple without recovery — EMERGENCY
causes: Neurocysticercosis (Taenia solium larva in brain — very common in India)
treatments: First-line: Sodium Valproate (generalised), Carbamazepine/Oxcarbazepine (focal)
Second-line: Levetiracetam, Lamotrigine, Phenytoin
Acute seizure: Diazepam IV/rectal OR Midazolam intranasal/buccal
Status epilepticus: IV lorazepam → Phenytoin → Phenobarbitone → general anaesthesia
Neurocysticercosis: Albendazole + Praziquantel + steroid cover
prevention: No specific prevention for genetic epilepsy
Prevent cysticercosis: hygiene, cooked pork, safe water
red_flags: Post-seizure weakness lasting >24h (Todd's palsy vs stroke)

general_diseases.name: Meningitis
general_diseases.description: Inflammation of meninges (brain coverings) — a medical emergency. Bacterial meningitis can be fatal within 24 hours. TB meningitis common in India. Classic triad: fever + headache + neck stiffness.
symptoms: Classic triad: fever + severe headache + neck stiffness (meningism)
Meningococcal: non-blanching petechial/purpuric rash (doesn't fade with glass tumbler test — EMERGENCY)
TB meningitis: more insidious onset, cranial nerve palsies, hydrocephalus
causes: Bacterial: Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Listeria (immunocompromised/elderly), Haemophilus
treatments: EMERGENCY — IV antibiotics IMMEDIATELY, do not wait for LP if CT/LP delayed
Bacterial: IV Ceftriaxone 2g 12-hourly + Dexamethasone (reduces complications)
Add Amoxicillin for Listeria (elderly, immunocompromised)
TB meningitis: standard anti-TB + high-dose steroids (Dexamethasone 0.4mg/kg/day)
Viral (HSV): IV Acyclovir 10mg/kg 8-hourly
Cryptococcal (HIV): Amphotericin B + Flucytosine
prevention: BCG vaccine (partial protection against TB meningitis)
Treat contacts of meningococcal: Rifampicin prophylaxis

general_diseases.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
general_diseases.description: Chronic metabolic disorder with insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency. India is the diabetes capital — 77 million diabetics. Indians develop T2DM a decade earlier than Western populations at lower BMI. Major cause of kidney failure, blindness, amputation, and heart disease.
symptoms: Classic triad: Polydipsia (increased thirst), Polyuria (frequent urination), Polyphagia (increased hunger)
causes: Insulin resistance (cells don't respond to insulin)
Risk factors: obesity (especially central adiposity), family history, sedentary lifestyle, high-carbohydrate diet, gestational diabetes history, PCOS
treatments: Lifestyle: Low GI diet (reduce rice/white flour), regular exercise (30 min/day), weight loss
First-line: Metformin 500-2000mg daily
SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin, Dapagliflozin — excellent, reduce CV and renal risk)
GLP-1 agonists (Semaglutide — Ozempic/Rybelsus — now available in India)
DPP4 inhibitors (Sitagliptin, Vildagliptin)
Sulphonylureas (Glibenclamide, Glipizide)
Insulin (multiple regimens for advanced disease)
Monitor: HbA1c every 3 months, annual eye screening, kidney function, foot exam
prevention: Lifestyle modification (weight loss 5-7% prevents onset by 58% in pre-diabetes)
red_flags: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA — vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath)

general_diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
general_diseases.description: Underactive thyroid with insufficient thyroid hormone production. India has 42 million hypothyroid patients. Extremely common in women. Iodine deficiency (common in inland areas) and autoimmune Hashimoto's are main causes.
symptoms: Dry skin and hair, hair loss
causes: Hashimoto's autoimmune thyroiditis (most common in non-deficient areas)
Iodine deficiency (endemic goitre in inland regions of India)
treatments: Levothyroxine (T4) replacement — start 25-50mcg, adjust to TSH target of 0.5-2.5 mIU/L
Take on empty stomach 30-60 min before breakfast
Lifelong treatment (usually)
Thyronorm and Eltroxin most common brands in India
Dose adjustment in pregnancy (increases by 30-50%)
Separate from calcium, iron, antacids (reduce absorption)
prevention: Iodine fortification (iodised salt — national programme in India)
Screening in pregnancy and neonates (national programme)
red_flags: Myxoedema coma (severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, unconsciousness — rare, emergency)
During pregnancy: foetal brain development risk

general_diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism / Graves' Disease
general_diseases.scientific_name: Hyperthyroidism / Graves' disease / Toxic nodular goitre
general_diseases.description: Overactive thyroid producing excess thyroid hormones. Graves' disease (autoimmune) most common in young women. Toxic multinodular goitre common in iodine-deficient areas of India.
causes: Graves' disease (TSH receptor antibody stimulates thyroid)
treatments: Anti-thyroid drugs: Carbimazole or Propylthiouracil (PTU)
Beta-blocker (Propranolol) for symptom control (tremor, palpitations)
Radioiodine ablation (I-131) — definitive
Thyroidectomy — definitive, especially for large goitre
Graves' ophthalmopathy: IV steroids, orbital radiotherapy, decompression
prevention: Regular thyroid function monitoring if on amiodarone or lithium

general_diseases.name: Malaria
general_diseases.description: Parasitic disease transmitted by Anopheles mosquito. India has ~1-2 million cases annually. P. vivax most common in India; P. falciparum causes severe disease and death. Highly endemic in states like Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand.
symptoms: Classic malarial paroxysm: cold/shivering phase → hot/fever phase → sweating phase (every 48-72h)
Severe malaria (P. falciparum): cerebral malaria (confusion, coma), severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia, ARDS, renal failure, DIC
causes: Plasmodium parasites (P. falciparum, vivax, malariae, ovale)
Female Anopheles mosquito bite (dusk to dawn biting)
treatments: P. vivax: Chloroquine 600mg then 300mg at 6h, 24h, 48h + Primaquine 15mg daily for 14 days (check G6PD before primaquine)
P. falciparum uncomplicated: Artemether-Lumefantrine (Coartem) for 3 days (WHO recommended) OR Artesunate + Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine as per India national protocol
Severe malaria: IV Artesunate (hospital) — superior to quinine
Chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum: ACT mandatory
prevention: Prophylaxis for travellers to endemic areas: Chloroquine, Doxycycline, or Mefloquine

general_diseases.name: Dengue Fever
general_diseases.description: Mosquito-borne viral infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquito. Massive epidemic in India — 200,000+ reported annually, actual cases estimated 10x higher. Dengue haemorrhagic fever and shock syndrome are life-threatening.
symptoms: Severe muscle and joint pain ('breakbone fever')
Warning signs for severe dengue: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, lethargy
Dengue shock: hypothermia, rapid pulse, narrow pulse pressure
causes: Aedes aegypti mosquito (day-biting, breeds in clean stagnant water — coolers, tanks, flower pots)
Second infection with different serotype → severe dengue
treatments: Symptomatic only (no specific antiviral)
Paracetamol for fever (NEVER aspirin or ibuprofen — bleeding risk)
Oral rehydration
Monitor platelet count and haematocrit daily
Platelet transfusion if <20,000 with bleeding or <10,000 absolute
Hospitalise if warning signs develop
Dengvaxia vaccine (for seropositive individuals — limited availability in India)
prevention: Eliminate mosquito breeding sites (empty water containers)
Aedes bites during daytime — protection during day essential

general_diseases.name: Leptospirosis
general_diseases.description: Zoonotic bacterial infection from rat urine-contaminated water. Very common in India during monsoon season — flooding in Mumbai, Chennai causes major outbreaks. Can cause severe Weil's disease (jaundice + renal failure + bleeding).
symptoms: Fever, headache, myalgia — flu-like phase (first week)
Second phase (immune): Weil's disease — jaundice, renal failure, hepatomegaly, bleeding, pulmonary haemorrhage, meningitis
causes: Contact with contaminated water (wading through flood water during monsoon)
Occupational: sewage workers, farmers, abattoir workers
treatments: Mild: Oral Doxycycline 100mg twice daily for 7 days
Severe Weil's disease: IV Benzylpenicillin 1.5MU 6-hourly for 7 days OR IV Ceftriaxone
Dialysis for severe renal failure
Manage haemorrhage
prevention: Avoid wading in flood water (or use rubber boots)
Doxycycline prophylaxis 200mg weekly for at-risk workers
Vaccination for high-risk groups (India has veterinary vaccine, human vaccine limited)

general_diseases.name: Depression
general_diseases.description: Serious mental health condition affecting mood, cognition, and behaviour. India has 56 million people suffering from depression. Significantly underdiagnosed and undertreated due to stigma. Major cause of suicide.
symptoms: Loss of interest or pleasure in activities (anhedonia)
Recurrent thoughts of death or suicide
causes: Multifactorial: genetic predisposition, neurochemical (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine)
Life events: loss, trauma, abuse, chronic illness
treatments: Psychotherapy: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) — gold standard
Antidepressants: SSRIs (Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Escitalopram) — first line; SNRIs (Venlafaxine)
TCAs (Amitriptyline) — cheaper, used in India for mild-moderate
Mirtazapine for sleep + appetite
Combination therapy (medication + psychotherapy) most effective
Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) for severe treatment-resistant depression
Lifestyle: exercise, social support, sleep hygiene
prevention: Early treatment of stress and trauma

general_diseases.name: Anxiety Disorders
general_diseases.scientific_name: Generalised Anxiety Disorder / Panic Disorder / Social Anxiety
general_diseases.description: Group of mental health conditions involving excessive fear and worry. Very common — affects 40 million globally. In India, anxiety often presents with somatic symptoms (palpitations, chest tightness, dizziness) and is frequently misdiagnosed as cardiac disease.
symptoms: GAD: Excessive worry about multiple areas, difficult to control, >6 months
Panic attack: Sudden intense fear with: palpitations, sweating, trembling, chest pain, breathlessness, dizziness, feeling of impending doom/unreality — peaks in 10 min
Social anxiety: intense fear of social situations, performance anxiety
Physical: headache, fatigue, GI symptoms, muscle tension
causes: Medical conditions (hyperthyroidism, cardiac arrhythmia — exclude first)
treatments: Psychotherapy: CBT is gold standard for all anxiety disorders
Exposure therapy for phobias/OCD
Medications: SSRIs (Escitalopram, Sertraline) — first line
SNRIs (Venlafaxine)
Buspirone (GAD)
Short-term benzodiazepines (Clonazepam, Alprazolam) — avoid long-term due to dependence
Beta-blocker (Propranolol) for performance anxiety
Lifestyle: exercise, yoga, mindfulness — very effective
red_flags: Panic attacks that prevent normal functioning

general_diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
general_diseases.description: Bacterial infection of the urinary tract. Extremely common, especially in women — 50% of women will have a UTI in their lifetime. Recurrent UTI is a common complaint in India. Complicated UTI (pyelonephritis) requires hospital treatment.
symptoms: Pyelonephritis: fever, loin/back pain, nausea, rigors — systemic infection
causes: Risk factors in women: short urethra, sexual intercourse ('honeymoon cystitis'), menopause (decreased oestrogen)
treatments: Uncomplicated lower UTI (women): Nitrofurantoin 100mg MR twice daily for 5 days OR Trimethoprim 200mg twice daily for 7 days OR Co-trimoxazole for 3 days
Check local resistance patterns (Ciprofloxacin resistance high in India)
Pyelonephritis: oral Ciprofloxacin 500mg twice daily for 7-14 days OR IV Ceftriaxone for hospitalised
Increase fluid intake
Treat underlying causes
prevention: Prophylactic low-dose antibiotics for recurrent UTI

general_diseases.name: Kidney Stones (Urolithiasis)
general_diseases.description: Crystalline mineral deposits in the urinary tract. Very common in India — 'Stone Belt' in northern India (Rajasthan, UP, MP) has very high prevalence. Dehydration from heat is a major risk factor.
symptoms: Renal colic: severe, colicky loin-to-groin pain (can be worst pain experienced)
Urinary frequency/urgency when stone at vesico-ureteric junction
Pale, sweaty, unable to find comfortable position
causes: Calcium oxalate stones (most common in India — 70%)
Uric acid stones (gout, high protein diet)
Risk factors: low fluid intake, hot climate (dehydration), high protein/oxalate/salt diet, family history, recurrent UTI
treatments: Analgesia: Diclofenac 75mg IM or IV (NSAID most effective), Morphine for severe
Alpha-blocker (Tamsulosin 0.4mg) aids passage of stones <10mm
Stones <5mm: usually pass spontaneously with hydration
Stones 5-10mm: ESWL (Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy)
Stones >10mm or obstructing: Ureteroscopy or PCNL (Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy)
Treat infection (UTI + obstruction = emergency — IV antibiotics + drainage)
prevention: Drink 2-3L fluid daily (most important — keeps urine dilute)
Reduce salt, protein, oxalate-rich foods (spinach, nuts, chocolate) for calcium oxalate stones
Potassium citrate for recurrent stone formers
red_flags: Stone with infection (pyonephrosis) — EMERGENCY, IV antibiotics + drainage

general_diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
general_diseases.description: Chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis causing joint destruction if untreated. Affects 0.5-1% of India's population. Women 3x more affected. Early diagnosis and treatment prevents permanent disability.
symptoms: Symmetrical small joint polyarthritis (MCP, PIP joints of hands, wrists, feet MTPs)
Systemic features: fatigue, low-grade fever, weight loss
Extra-articular: rheumatoid nodules, dry eyes/mouth, pleural effusion, cardiac involvement
Ulnar deviation, swan neck, boutonnière deformity (late untreated)
causes: Autoimmune — anti-CCP antibody and RF-mediated synovitis
Oestrogen role (more common in women, improves in pregnancy)
treatments: Early aggressive treatment prevents joint damage
DMARDs: Methotrexate (most important — first line) 7.5-25mg weekly
Hydroxychloroquine, Sulfasalazine, Leflunomide
Biologics (if DMARDs fail): TNF inhibitors (Etanercept, Adalimumab), IL-6 inhibitor (Tocilizumab), JAK inhibitors (Baricitinib, Tofacitinib)
NSAIDs and steroids for symptom control only
Physiotherapy
prevention: Smoking cessation reduces risk and improves drug response
Early diagnosis and treatment prevents disability

general_diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
general_diseases.description: Degenerative joint disease — most common arthritis, especially in elderly. Knee OA is epidemic in India — heavy physical labour, sitting cross-legged (squatting), and obesity are key contributing factors. Leading cause of disability in older Indians.
symptoms: Joint pain worsening with activity, better with rest
Knee, hip, lumbar spine, hands most commonly affected in India
Heberden's (DIP) and Bouchard's (PIP) nodes in hand OA
causes: Risk factors: obesity (increases knee load significantly), previous joint injury, repetitive occupational stress (farmers — squatting), family history
treatments: Weight loss (most effective intervention for knee OA — 1kg weight loss = 4kg less knee load)
Exercise: quadriceps strengthening (key for knee OA), low-impact aerobics, physiotherapy
Paracetamol (first-line analgesic)
Topical NSAIDs (Diclofenac gel)
Oral NSAIDs for moderate-severe (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac — with gastroprotection)
Intra-articular steroid injection
Knee replacement (TKR) — when conservative measures fail
prevention: Avoid prolonged squatting (modify Indian toilet usage if possible)
red_flags: Septic arthritis (hot, very painful, swollen joint with fever — EMERGENCY)
warning_signs: Hot swollen joint with fever (septic arthritis)

general_diseases.name: Gout
general_diseases.description: Uric acid crystal deposition causing exquisitely painful acute arthritis. Incidence rising in India with dietary changes (meat, alcohol, fructose consumption increasing). First metatarsophalangeal joint (big toe) is classic site.
symptoms: Acute attack: exquisite pain, redness, swelling, warmth in one joint (usually first MTP — big toe)
Unable to tolerate even bedsheet on joint
Tophi: hard deposits of uric acid under skin (chronic)
causes: Dietary purines: red meat, organ meats, shellfish, beer, fructose
treatments: Acute attack: NSAIDs (Indomethacin 50mg TID or Naproxen) OR Colchicine 500mcg TID OR Short-course Prednisolone
Long-term urate-lowering: Allopurinol (start at 100mg, titrate to uric acid <360umol/L) — do NOT start during acute attack
Febuxostat (alternative to allopurinol)
Dietary modification (reduce red meat, beer, fructose; increase low-fat dairy, vegetables)
Adequate hydration
red_flags: Septic arthritis (exclude in any hot swollen joint)
warning_signs: Extremely hot swollen joint (septic arthritis vs gout — hospital)

general_diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anaemia
general_diseases.description: Most common nutritional deficiency worldwide. India has highest burden — 50% of women and 25% of men. Major cause: poor dietary iron intake, vegetarian diet (non-haem iron poorly absorbed), malnutrition, hookworm infestation, menorrhagia.
symptoms: Pica (craving for non-food items: ice, mud — common in India)
causes: Blood loss: menorrhagia (very common in Indian women), GI bleeding, hookworm infestation
Poor absorption: coeliac disease, post-gastric surgery
treatments: Oral iron: Ferrous Sulphate 200mg (65mg elemental iron) twice-three times daily — for 3-6 months (2 months to correct Hb, 4 more to replenish stores)
Take on empty stomach with vitamin C for better absorption
IV iron (Ferric Carboxymaltose) for malabsorption or intolerance
Treat underlying cause (menorrhagia, hookworm)
Diet: increase non-vegetarian sources (chicken, fish, red meat), or iron-fortified foods; include vitamin C with meals
prevention: Iron supplementation during pregnancy (national programme in India)
red_flags: Underlying GI malignancy causing blood loss
warning_signs: Hb very low with breathlessness at rest

general_diseases.name: Sickle Cell Disease
general_diseases.description: Hereditary haemoglobin disorder with chronic haemolytic anaemia and vaso-occlusive crises. High prevalence in central Indian tribal populations (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Odisha — up to 33% carrier rate in some communities). Major health priority.
symptoms: Vaso-occlusive (painful) crises: severe bone/joint/abdominal pain — precipitated by cold, infection, dehydration, stress
Acute chest syndrome: chest pain + fever + breathlessness (life-threatening)
Splenic sequestration (children): sudden spleen engorgement, shock
causes: Homozygous HbSS (sickle cell disease) or compound heterozygote (HbSC, HbS-beta thal)
treatments: Crisis: IV fluids, opioid analgesia (morphine), oxygen, treat precipitants
Hydroxyurea 15-30mg/kg/day (reduces crises, extends life)
Transfusion for acute chest, stroke, severe anaemia
Penicillin prophylaxis (asplenic — daily for children)
Pneumococcal, Haemophilus, Meningococcal vaccines
Stem cell transplantation (curative — selected patients)
Gene therapy (clinical trials)
Folic acid supplementation
prevention: Newborn screening (national programme expanding in India)
red_flags: Aplastic crisis (B19 parvovirus — rapid fall in Hb)

general_diseases.name: Glaucoma
general_diseases.description: Progressive optic nerve damage from raised intraocular pressure (IOP) causing irreversible visual field loss. India has ~12 million glaucoma patients. A leading cause of irreversible blindness. Often silent until late stage.
symptoms: Open-angle (chronic): Often asymptomatic until advanced; gradual peripheral vision loss (tunnel vision)
Angle-closure (acute): Sudden severe eye pain, headache, nausea, halos around lights, red eye, blurred vision — EMERGENCY
Risk factors: high IOP, family history, age, thin cornea
causes: Raised intraocular pressure (IOP >21mmHg) damaging optic nerve
Secondary: steroids (very important — steroid-induced glaucoma from misuse of eye drops in India), trauma, inflammation
treatments: Eye drops to lower IOP: prostaglandin analogue (Latanoprost — first-line), beta-blocker (Timolol), CAI (Dorzolamide/Brinzolamide)
Laser: SLT (selective laser trabeculoplasty) for OAG, laser iridotomy for angle-closure
Surgery: trabeculectomy for advanced/uncontrolled
Acute angle closure: Pilocarpine + Timolol + IV Acetazolamide + urgent laser iridotomy
prevention: Regular eye pressure checks (especially if family history, age >40, diabetic)
Avoid steroid eye drops without prescription (common in India — causes steroid glaucoma)
Yoga/Inversion positions can raise IOP — caution in glaucoma
red_flags: Acute angle closure (EMERGENCY — same-day treatment needed)

general_diseases.name: Diabetic Retinopathy
general_diseases.description: Microvascular complication of diabetes causing progressive retinal damage. Leading cause of blindness in working-age adults. India has massive burden — with 77 million diabetics, millions have retinopathy. Often completely asymptomatic until vision-threatening stage.
symptoms: Sudden vision loss (vitreous haemorrhage or retinal detachment)
Dark or empty areas in vision
causes: Risk factors: long duration of diabetes, poor glycaemic control, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, nephropathy
treatments: Optimise blood sugar control (HbA1c <7%)
Control blood pressure
VEGF inhibitors (Ranibizumab, Bevacizumab) for diabetic macular oedema — intravitreal injection
Laser photocoagulation for proliferative retinopathy
Vitrectomy for vitreous haemorrhage/tractional retinal detachment
prevention: Annual dilated eye exam for all diabetics
red_flags: Sudden vision loss (retinal detachment, vitreous haemorrhage — EMERGENCY)

general_diseases.name: Measles
general_diseases.description: Highly contagious viral infection. Major cause of child mortality globally. India still sees outbreaks in unvaccinated communities. Complications (pneumonia, encephalitis, malnutrition) kill. Vaccine-preventable.
symptoms: Prodrome: high fever, cough, coryza (runny nose), conjunctivitis (3Cs)
Koplik's spots (pathognomonic): white spots on inner cheek, appear before rash
Maculopapular rash: starts behind ears/hairline, spreads to face → trunk → extremities
Rash appears as fever peaks then descends
Complications: pneumonia, otitis media, diarrhoea, encephalitis, SSPE (rare)
causes: Highly contagious — airborne, 90% attack rate in non-immune
treatments: Supportive: antipyretics, hydration, vitamin A (WHO recommendation — reduces mortality)
Vitamin A 200,000 IU for 2 days (reduces complications)
Antibiotics for bacterial complications (pneumonia, otitis media)
Hospital for complications
prevention: MMR vaccine (2 doses: 9 months and 15-18 months in India)
red_flags: Severe malnutrition + measles = very high mortality

general_diseases.name: Dengue in Children
general_diseases.description: Dengue in children often presents atypically and can progress rapidly to severe dengue/shock. Dengue is a leading cause of child hospitalisation in India.
symptoms: Warning signs: persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, bleeding, irritability or lethargy
Dengue shock: cold extremities, rapid weak pulse, narrow pulse pressure
treatments: Paracetamol only for fever (NEVER aspirin or ibuprofen)
Careful oral hydration
Hospitalise if warning signs
Close monitoring of platelet and haematocrit

general_diseases.name: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)
general_diseases.description: Most common endocrine disorder in reproductive-age women. Prevalence 3.7-22.5% in Indian women. Key features: menstrual irregularity, hyperandrogenism (excess male hormones), and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound. Associated with insulin resistance, T2DM, cardiovascular risk.
symptoms: Hirsutism (excess facial/body hair — along male pattern)
treatments: Lifestyle: weight loss (5-10% weight loss restores cycles in obese PCOS — most effective)
Metformin (reduces insulin resistance, restores ovulation)
Combined OCP (Ethinylestradiol + anti-androgen: cyproterone acetate, drospirenone) — for menstrual regulation and hirsutism
Spironolactone (anti-androgen) for hirsutism
Clomiphene citrate or Letrozole for ovulation induction (fertility)
Eflornithine cream for facial hair
Inositol (evidence growing)
prevention: Early management prevents progression to T2DM
red_flags: Pregnancy with uncontrolled PCOS (gestational diabetes risk)
warning_signs: Very irregular periods with PCOS (endometrial protection needed)

general_diseases.name: Breast Cancer
general_diseases.description: Most common cancer in Indian women (25.8% of female cancers). India presents at later stages due to stigma, lack of screening, and limited access. Most are hormone receptor positive (ER+/PR+). 5-year survival dramatically improves with early detection.
symptoms: Change in breast shape or size
Skin changes over breast (peau d'orange, dimpling)
causes: Hormonal factors: early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, late first pregnancy, OCP/HRT use
treatments: Surgery: lumpectomy or mastectomy with sentinel/axillary node biopsy
Radiotherapy (post-surgery)
Hormone therapy: Tamoxifen (pre-menopausal ER+), Aromatase inhibitor (post-menopausal: Letrozole, Anastrozole)
Chemotherapy (neoadjuvant or adjuvant)
Targeted therapy: Trastuzumab (Herceptin) for HER2+
CDK4/6 inhibitors (Palbociclib) for metastatic ER+ disease
red_flags: Inflammatory breast cancer (red, hot, swollen breast — aggressive)
Very young patient with breast lump
warning_signs: Any new breast lump — needs urgent assessment

general_diseases.name: Allergic Rhinitis
general_diseases.description: IgE-mediated inflammation of nasal mucosa from allergen exposure. Extremely common in India — 20-30% prevalence. Parthenium weed (Congress grass) is a unique and major allergen in India. Strongly associated with asthma (united airways).
symptoms: Seasonal (pollen, Parthenium in India) or perennial (dust mites, pet dander)
causes: Allergens in India: House dust mites (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus — most common), Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress grass — VERY common in India), cockroach, pollen (grass, trees, weeds), cat/dog dander, mould
treatments: Intranasal corticosteroids (Mometasone, Fluticasone) — most effective for moderate-severe
Non-sedating antihistamines (Cetirizine, Fexofenadine, Loratadine)
Intranasal antihistamine (Azelastine)
Combination: intranasal corticosteroid + antihistamine for severe
Allergen avoidance (dust mite covers, avoid Parthenium contact)
Allergen immunotherapy (desensitisation) — suitable for selected patients
Saline nasal rinse (Jal Neti — traditional Indian practice, evidence-based)

general_diseases.name: Acute Tonsillitis / Pharyngitis
general_diseases.description: Inflammation of tonsils and throat. Very common in India especially in children. Group A Streptococcal (GAS) pharyngitis is important to treat to prevent rheumatic heart disease (still prevalent in India).
symptoms: Absence of cough (suggests bacterial rather than viral)
causes: Bacterial: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) — 20-40% in children (most important to treat)
treatments: Viral: Symptomatic — analgesia, hydration, salt water gargles
GAS Bacterial: Phenoxymethylpenicillin (Penicillin V) 500mg twice daily for 10 days OR Amoxicillin 500mg twice daily for 10 days (BUT avoid if EBV suspected — causes widespread rash)
Penicillin allergy: Erythromycin or Clarithromycin for 10 days
Dexamethasone (single dose) significantly reduces symptom duration
Recurrent tonsillitis (>7 in 1 year, or >5 per year for 2 years): tonsillectomy
prevention: Early treatment of GAS prevents rheumatic fever (RHD prevention)
red_flags: Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy): unilateral swelling, 'hot potato' voice, drooling, difficulty opening mouth — surgical drainage needed
EBV mononucleosis with massive spleen (avoid contact sports — rupture risk)
warning_signs: Unable to swallow or open mouth (quinsy)
Muffled voice with severe throat swelling

general_diseases.name: Rosacea
general_diseases.description: Chronic facial skin condition with redness, papules, and telangiectasia. More common in fair-skinned individuals but increasingly recognised in Indian skin. Triggers include heat, alcohol, spicy food, sun exposure.
symptoms: Persistent facial redness (centrofacial — cheeks, nose, forehead, chin)
Papules and pustules (acne-like but NO blackheads/whiteheads)
Flushing episodes triggered by heat, alcohol, spicy food, sun
causes: Multifactorial: vascular dysregulation, Demodex mite overgrowth, immune dysregulation, skin barrier dysfunction
Triggers: sun, heat, alcohol, spicy food, stress, certain cosmetics
treatments: Topical: Metronidazole gel 0.75-1%, Azelaic acid 15-20%, Ivermectin 1% cream (anti-Demodex)
Oral: Doxycycline 40mg modified-release (low dose anti-inflammatory effect)
Laser and IPL (intense pulsed light) for telangiectasia
Brimonidine topical gel for redness
Sun protection mandatory
red_flags: Ocular rosacea with eye involvement (ophthalmology referral)

general_diseases.name: Lichen Planus
general_diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory skin condition with characteristic violaceous flat-topped papules. Affects skin, mucous membranes, nails, and scalp. Hepatitis C association important. Common in middle-aged Indian adults.
symptoms: Wickham's striae (white lacy pattern on surface of papules/mucosa)
Distribution: flexor wrists, lower legs, lower back, genitals, oral mucosa
Oral: white lacy patches or erosive (painful)
treatments: Topical corticosteroids (potent betamethasone)
Oral: Prednisolone short course for widespread eruption
Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus) for oral/genital lichen planus
Retinoids (acitretin) for widespread/resistant
Phototherapy (NB-UVB)
Hydroxychloroquine
red_flags: Erosive oral lichen planus (malignant transformation risk — rare)

general_diseases.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
general_diseases.description: Severe autoimmune blistering disease affecting skin and mucous membranes. Higher prevalence in South Asians and those of Jewish/Iranian descent. Potentially life-threatening without treatment. Mucosal involvement (painful oral ulcers) often precedes skin blisters.
symptoms: Painful oral ulcers/erosions (typically first symptom — months before skin)
Flaccid (thin-walled, easily rupturing) blisters on skin
Erosions (blisters rupture quickly, leaving raw areas)
Nikolsky sign positive (gentle pressure extends blisters laterally)
causes: Anti-desmoglein 3 (oral) and 1 (skin) antibodies damaging keratinocyte adhesion
treatments: Hospitalise for extensive disease
Prednisolone 1mg/kg/day (induction)
Rituximab (anti-CD20 — dramatically changed outcomes, now first-line in severe cases)
Azathioprine or Mycophenolate mofetil (steroid-sparing)
Dapsone (adjunct)
Wound care for erosions
